title: VERIFY T-436: attack the contracts design before the operator reads it
description: Adversarial read of .harness/design-T-436-contracts.md. Try 4 attacks and write each result next to its section: (1) a damage that is in fact computed from a figure about an identity, so constitutional under PR-060 clause 5; (2) a path where repeated damages exclude an agent by computed standing (PR-026 clause 3); (3) a consequence with no record of its own (PR-060 clause 6); (4) a claim cheap enough to be used as a weapon. Check every cited clause against the record text in .harness/precedents/. Verdict done only if every attack has a written answer and the document says what stays open.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the 4 attacks was run and its result is written on the board next to the section it targets.
Every clause the design cites was checked against .harness/precedents/ and any miscitation is named.
Verdict recorded on the board with the checks replayed, not copied from the thinker's note.

notes.note:
VERIFIED (round 4): design-T-436-contracts.md passes all 4 attacks and the clause-citation check, replayed independently and by a method the producer did not use (static read of attest.py's actual sign_act/contest/declare_intent/_match_intent/intent_binds_ref code, not document-only citation checking).

Attack (1) identity-figure damage -- no success. Section 3's forfeiture debit and section 5's claim-disposition records are each computed from one task's own committed-vs-observed value; no aggregation across tasks or by name; confirmed against PR-060.json validity_conditions: "No harness store holds a stored standing or balance field, so no figure can become an operational parameter by accident." Holds, unchanged from rounds 1-3.

Attack (2) PR-026 c3 exclusion by computed standing -- no success. No running per-name count exists anywhere in the design. Confirmed PR-026.json ratio clause 3 verbatim: "No automatic demotion, suspension or exclusion of any identity by computed standing alone." Section 3's second cap (debit bounded against the next task's own allocation, ratio left to the operator) closes round-1's starvation caveat without importing a standing computation. Holds.

Attack (3) consequence with no record of its own -- no success. Section 4: "This is the one record format for every consequence named here: section 3's forfeiture, the priority bump, and a section 5 claim's disposition... A claim REFUSED at filing... produces no record under this format, and no attest.py act of any kind." A non-consequence needing no record is consistent with PR-060 clause 6 (confirmed verbatim against PR-060.json: "Every individual consequence still requires its own published record"). Holds.

Attack (4) cheap claim as weapon -- re-run against the NEW mechanism (file_claim / replay-at-filing), not the retired price formula, per dispatch instruction. Read attest.py's actual code, not just the design's gloss of it:
- sign_act() (attest.py line ~662-730): the comment quoted in the design, "It still refuses before any file is created, so a refusal writes nothing" (verified verbatim at line 730), sits immediately before the file-creation step (os.open with O_CREAT|O_EXCL at line ~744). A new committed-vs-observed check inserted at that point, before os.open, would indeed write nothing on a no-gap outcome -- the design's claim is architecturally sound, not just asserted.
- I additionally traced a vector NOT covered by rounds 1-3: contest is a PRIVILEGED_KINDS entry (line 144), so D3a requires an open intent to already exist before sign_act(kind="contest") can succeed (_match_intent, line 620). I checked whether this intent-declaration precondition forces a respondent-naming record to be written before/regardless of the gap-check (which would reopen round 3's exact bug through a different act type). It does NOT, by construction: intent_binds_ref (line 588) lets an intent with an empty for_ref bind to ANY target of that kind+task ("an intent that leaves for_ref empty constrains kind and task only"), and nothing requires the intent to be declared before the gap-check -- a correct file_claim can declare the intent (with empty for_ref, or just-in-time) only inside the gap-confirmed branch, immediately before calling contest, so a REFUSED claim calls neither declare_intent nor contest and writes nothing, matching the design's own required invariant ("write-nothing-on-no-gap," listed as an explicit, not-yet-built property in section 6).
- This is a genuine, non-blocking WEAKNESS to flag, not a successful attack against the document as written: the design is silent on this D3a/intent interaction (the producer's own handoff note flagged it as unresolved, "I did not have time/scope to trace this fully and it is not mentioned in the revised document"), so a careless future implementation COULD reintroduce round-3's bug via an intent act instead of a contest act, if it pre-declares an intent naming the target before checking the gap. The design's stated invariant is achievable, so this is a documentation/specification gap for the eventual worker task to close explicitly, not a contradiction in the text itself.
- Beyond that: the two residuals the document discloses (FORGERY -- forging the observed source or the respondent's commit act, routed to D-17, not claimed closed; BYPASS -- calling attest.py's raw `contest` CLI verb directly instead of through file_claim, needing no forged key, not claimed closed until a worker task gates it) are both honestly stated as open in section 6, not claimed closed, consistent with the dispatch's rule that a forging-dependent residual counts as the D-17 limit only if disclosed honestly -- confirmed it is.
- No success: attack (4) does not find a claim that is cheap AND produces a respondent-naming record AND is forced by the mechanism as specified. The closest lever (the intent-declaration precondition) is avoidable by a correct implementation and is already scoped as unbuilt in section 6.

Miscitation check (replayed independently against .harness/precedents/*.json, attest.py's actual docstring/code, operator-rulings-2026-10-08.md, and docs/precedent-research/21-swiss-identity-and-enforcement.md):
- PR-060 clauses 1, 2, 5, 6 + all 4 scope_conditions + all 3 validity_conditions: verbatim match against .harness/precedents/PR-060.json's ratio/scope_conditions/validity_conditions fields.
- PR-022 clause 4: verbatim match against .harness/precedents/PR-022.json.
- PR-026 clause 3: verbatim match against .harness/precedents/PR-026.json ("No automatic demotion, suspension or exclusion of any identity by computed standing alone.").
- PR-061 clauses 1 and 3: verbatim match against .harness/precedents/PR-061.json ("claim priority queue ordering" is in clause 1 verbatim; clause 3's non-staking text matches verbatim).
- operator-rulings-2026-10-08.md: the "Adelante la idea..." and "a contract binds a name, not a proven agent" quotes confirmed verbatim at lines 34-35 (cat -n checked) -- round-2's miscitation (this quote had been wrongly attributed to design-T-432-agent-identity.md) is fixed; the design now correctly attributes it to operator-rulings-2026-10-08.md.
- The D-17 paraphrase ("every agent runs as the same OS user on one filesystem...") correctly traces to .harness/design-T-432-agent-identity.md's own text ("every agent runs as the same OS user on the same filesystem. There is no isolation boundary between agents, so no agent can hold a secret another agent cannot read") -- stated as a paraphrase, not a verbatim quote, so no miscitation.
- attest.py DIS-2, DIS-4, DIS-5, AF-3 quotes: verbatim match against attest.py's module docstring (grep-checked each).
- Swiss brief section 3 and section 8 items 2, 4, 5: verbatim match against docs/precedent-research/21-swiss-identity-and-enforcement.md lines 34-39, 83, 85-86.
- precedent.py case {open,list,show} claim checked against the actual CLI (`precedent.py case --help` lists open, list, show, publisher-report) -- accurate, named subset.
- No new miscitation found. Round-3's self-contradiction (the "no record naming the respondent" claim being false about the contest()-routed mechanism) is fixed by the new file_claim gate, confirmed against sign_act's actual guard structure.

Word count confirmed: wc -w = 3800, at the stated cap.

Hygiene: `git status --porcelain` shows only .harness/blackboard.json, .harness/tasks/T-436.json (claim/update mutations) and the new .harness/design-T-436-contracts.md -- nothing under .harness/trust, .harness/constitutional or .harness/keys. Blackboard task count confirmed unchanged at 233 (T-000..T-437), no new task ids created. `lock.py status`: no active locks. `lock.py sweep`: swept 0 expired locks.

Non-blocking weaknesses for the operator / round-5-or-worker-task to address before file_claim is built:
1. The D3a intent-declaration precondition for contest (a PRIVILEGED_KINDS entry) is not discussed anywhere in the design. It should explicitly require file_claim to declare any precondition intent with an empty for_ref and/or only inside the gap-confirmed branch, so the write-nothing-on-no-gap invariant the document already promises cannot be silently broken by a worker who instead pre-declares a target-naming intent before the gap-check.
2. The numeric schedule (debit ratios/ceiling, objection window, pursue-or-lapse window) remains entirely unset, as disclosed; the operator must ratify these before any worker task fixes them in code.
3. Decision 3 (who adjudicates a halted claim) is still named only as an interface, per the task's own instruction -- correctly left undesigned.

Verdict: ACCEPT. All 4 attacks run and answered; no miscitation found (round-2's is confirmed fixed); hygiene clean; acceptance criteria met. T-437 (verify T-436) closed with the same evidence.
